message.content:
Tycho Brahe was one of the most prominent critics, proposing his own geo-heliocentric system as a compromise. Cardinal Robert Bellarmine played a key role in the 1616 edict that placed *De Revolutionibus* on the Index of Forbidden Books. Pope Paul V formally condemned the heliocentric model in 1616, ordering that it be treated only as a mathematical hypothesis. Thomas More, in his 1516 work *Utopia*, mocked the heliocentric idea by having a character call it absurd.

Did the Church's opposition stem purely from scientific disagreement or from deeper theological concerns? How did Copernicus's own Polish contemporaries react to his heliocentric theory? Who were the other notable figures that challenged his work? What role did Aristotle's physics play in the rejection of heliocentrism?

What a bold challenge to centuries of accepted cosmology! The consequences of his work were truly revolutionary! How daring it was to overturn the entire medieval understanding of the universe! Imagine the intellectual shock of declaring that the Earth moves!
